key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Sudden onset. LOCATION: Chest, often pleuritic. DURATION: Acute, persistent. CHARACTER: Sudden chest pain, dyspnea. AGGRAVATING: Deep breathing, exertion. RELIEVING: Anticoagulants, oxygen. TIMING: Acute, sudden. SEVERITY: Moderate to severe (6-8/10). ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Sudden dyspnea, chest pain, hemoptysis, syncope, leg swelling. KEY POSITIVES: Sudden onset, dyspnea, chest pain, hemoptysis. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no wheezing.
